30
Q 33:59 · Vol. 3, pp. 559–560

Verse 59

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful. (59)
يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لِأَزْواجِكَ وَبَناتِكَ وَنِساءِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلابِيبِهِنَّ ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَنْ يُعْرَفْنَ فَلا يُؤْذَيْنَ وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً (59)
Vol. 3, p. 559
" The jilbāb: a wide garment, wider than the khimār and smaller than the ridāʾ, which a woman wraps over her head, leaving of it what she lets down over her chest. And from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both: it is the ridāʾ that covers from above to below.
الجلباب: ثوب واسع أوسع من الخمار ودون الرداء تلويه المرأة على رأسها وتبقى منه ما ترسله على صدرها. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: الرداء الذي يستر من فوق إلى أسفل.
Vol. 3, p. 560
It was also said: the milḥafa, and everything with which one covers oneself, whether a cloak or other than it. Abū Zubayd said: "clad in a jilbāb of the blackness of the night" (1). And the meaning of "to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments" is: they let them down over themselves and cover their faces and their sides with them. It is said, when the garment slips from the face of a woman: bring your garment down over your face. And that is because the women in the early period of Islam were, in their habitual way from the Jāhiliyya, in everyday undress: a woman would go out in a dirʿ and a khimār, with no distinction made between the free woman and the slave woman; and the young men and the rowdies would accost the slave girls when they went out at night to their errands among the palm groves and the low-lying fields, and at times they accosted the free woman on the pretext that she was a slave girl, saying: "We thought she was a slave girl." So they were commanded to differ in their appearance from the appearance of the slave girls by wearing cloaks and milḥafas and covering the heads and faces, so that they would be [seen as] modest and respected, and no covetous person would desire them; and that is His saying "That is more suitable that they will be known," that is, more fitting and apt that they be recognized, so that they are not accosted and do not meet what they dislike.
وقيل: الملحفة وكل ما يستتر به من كساء أو غيره. قال أبو زبيد: مجلبب من سواد اللّيل جلبابا «1» ومعنى يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلَابِيبِهِنَّ يرخينها عليهنّ، ويغطين بها وجوههنّ وأعطافهنّ. يقال: إذا زل الثوب عن وجه المرأة: أدنى ثوبك على وجهك، وذلك أن النساء كنّ في أول الإسلام على هجيراهنّ في الجاهلية متبذلات، تبرز المرأة في درع وخمار فصل بين الحرّة والأمة، وكان الفتيان وأهل الشطارة يتعرّضون إذا خرجن بالليل إلى مقاضى حوائجهنّ في النخيل والغيطان للإماء، وربما تعرّضوا للحرّه بعلة الأمة، يقولون: حسبناها أمة، فأمرن أن يخالفن بزيهنّ عن زى الإماء بلبس الأردية والملاحف وستر الرؤوس والوجوه، ليحتشمن ويهين فلا يطمع فيهن طامع، وذلك قوله ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَنْ يُعْرَفْنَ أى أولى وأجدر بأن يعرفن فلا يتعرّض لهن ولا يلقين ما يكرهن.
Question
If you ask: what is the meaning of "min" in "min jalābībihinna"?
فإن قلت: ما معنى مِنْ في مِنْ جَلَابِيبِهِنَّ؟
Answer
I say: it is partitive; but the partitive meaning admits of two aspects. One: that they wrap themselves in some of the jilbābs they possess, the intention being that the free woman not be in everyday undress in a dirʿ and a khimār like the slave girl and the servant while she has two jilbābs or more in her house. The second: that the woman let down some of her jilbāb, its surplus, over her face, covering herself (taqannaʿ) so that she is distinguished from the slave girl. And from Ibn Sīrīn: I asked ʿAbīda al-Salmānī about that and he said: that she place her ridāʾ above the brow, then wind it around until she places it over her nose. And from al-Suddī: that she cover one of her eyes and her forehead, and the other side except the eye. And from al-Kisāʾī: they cover themselves with their milḥafas drawn close around them; by "drawn close" he meant the sense of "bringing down." "And ever is God Forgiving" of what preceded from them of negligence, with repentance (2), because this is something whose knowledge is possible by reason.
قلت: هو للتبعيض، إلا أن معنى التبعيض محتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أن يتجلببن ببعض مالهنّ من الجلابيب، والمراد أن لا تكون الحرة متبذلة في درع وخمار، كالأمة والماهنة ولها جلبابان فصاعدا في بيتها. والثاني: أن ترخى المرأة بعض جلبابها وفضله على وجهها تتقنع حتى تتميز من الأمة. وعن ابن سيرين: سألت عبيدة السلماني عن ذلك فقال: أن تضع رداءها فوق الحاجب ثم تديره حتى تضعه على أنفها. وعن السدى: أن تغطى إحدى عينيها وجبهتها، والشق الآخر إلا العين. وعن الكسائي: يتقنعن بملاحفهن منضمة عليهنّ، أراد بالانضمام معنى الإدناء وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً لما سلف منهن من التفريط مع التوبة «2» ، لأن هذا مما يمكن معرفته بالعقل.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 559
1. (1). Narrated by al-Ṭabarī from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra ؓ; and from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both, to similar effect.
2. . "So how": the wording of al-Nasafī is: "so how [is] the harming of believing men and believing women." (ʿ)
1. (1) . أخرجه الطبري من حديث أبى هريرة رضى الله عنه. ومن حديث ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما نحوه.
2. . «فكيف» عبارة النسفي: فكيف إيذاء المؤمنين والمؤمنات. (ع)
Vol. 3, p. 560
1. (1). "Welcome to a guest who came to me whenever the door was sought to be opened (?), / Clad in a jilbāb of the blackness of the night" — by Abū Zubayd. "Ahlan" is the object of an obligatorily omitted verb, i.e., "I have come to a family"; "bi-ḍayf" is connected to an omitted [verb], i.e., "I welcome a guest"; it may also be connected to "ahlan," because it contains the sense of welcome. "Mā" is a verbal-noun particle, i.e., "for the duration of the door's remaining [open]"; the intention is generality, i.e., at whatever time the opening of the door is sought. He described him as the one who comes in the blackness of the night, as an exaggeration in praising generosity. It may also be [illegible in the source: ؟؟؟] that the guest is his beloved, in which case the night would have [illegible: ؟؟؟]. And he likened his guest's concealment by the darkness of the night to the wearing of clothing, and the figurative usage is in "jalbaba" or in "jilbāb," by way of explicit metaphor (taṣrīḥiyya). It is also possible [to read] "mā" as negative, in which case it may be an address to the Angel of Death, since he enters without asking for the door to be opened, although the guest and the beloved may also do that.
2. . His statement "of what preceded from them of negligence [lit. 'of their cursing'], with repentance" [sic, as printed]: this is according to the Muʿtazila; or by mere grace according to Ahl al-Sunna. (ʿ)
1. (1) . أهلا بضيف أنى ما استفتح البابا
…. مجلبب من سواد الليل جلبابا لأبى زبيد. وأهلا: مفعول لمحذوف وجوبا، أى: أتيت أهلا. وبضيف: متعلق بمحذوف، أى. أرحب بضيف: ويجوز تعلقه بأهلا، لأن فيه معنى الترحيب. وما: مصدرية، أى: مدة استقامة الباب. والمراد منه التعميم، أى: في أى وقت يطلب فتح الباب: وصفه بالآتى في سواد الليل، مبالغة في التمدح بالكرم. ويجوز؟؟؟ أن الضيف محبوبته، فيكون الليل استزلها؟؟؟. وشبه استتار ضيفه بظلام الليل يلبس اللباس، والتجوز في الجلببة أو في الجلباب على طريق التصريحية، ويجوز لأن ما نافية، وعلى هذا فيصح أن يكون خطابا لملك الموت، حيث دخل ولم يطلب فتح الباب، وإن كان الضيف والحبيب قد يفعلان ذلك أيضا
2. . قوله «لما سلف لعنهن من التفريط مع التوبة» هذا عند المعتزلة. أو بمجرد الفضل عند أهل السنة. (ع)
31
Q 33:60–62 · Vol. 3, pp. 560–562

Verses 60 to 62

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease and those who spread rumors in the city do not cease, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little, (60) Accursed wherever they are found, seized and massacred completely. (61) [That is] the established way of God with those who passed on before; and you will never find in the way of God any change. (62)
لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْمُرْجِفُونَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ ثُمَّ لا يُجاوِرُونَكَ فِيها إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً (60) مَلْعُونِينَ أَيْنَما ثُقِفُوا أُخِذُوا وَقُتِّلُوا تَقْتِيلاً (61) سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ فِي الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلاً (62)
Vol. 3, p. 560
"
Vol. 3, p. 561
"Those in whose hearts is disease": a people in whom there was weakness of faith and little steadfastness in it. It was also said: they are the fornicators and the people of depravity, from His saying Most High "lest he in whose heart is disease should covet." "And those who spread rumors": people who used to spread bad news about the expeditions of the Messenger of God ﷺ saying: "They were defeated and killed, and such-and-such happened to them," thereby breaking the hearts of the believers. It is said "arjafa bi-kadhā" when one reports it not as it truly is, because it is wavering, unestablished news, from "rajfa," which is a quaking. And the meaning: if the hypocrites do not cease from their enmity and plotting against you, and the transgressors from their depravity, and the rumor-mongers from what they concoct of bad news, "We will surely command you to do to them the deeds that distress them and weigh heavily upon them" (1), and then to compel them to seek exile from Medina and to not dwell with you in it "except for a little" — a short time, just long enough for them to depart and gather up themselves and their dependents (2). So He called that "inciting," which is egging on, by way of figurative usage. "Accursed": accusative as an expression of reviling or as a circumstantial qualifier, that is: they will not neighbor you except accursed; the particle of exception entered upon the adverbial and the circumstantial together, as occurred earlier in His saying "except when you are permitted to a meal, without awaiting its readiness." And it is not valid for it to be accusative as governed by "they are seized," because what follows the particle of condition does not act upon what precedes it. And it was said regarding "qalīlan" that it is also accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, its meaning being: they will not neighbor you except as few, humiliated, accursed ones.
الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ قوم كان فيهم ضعف إيمان وقلة ثبات عليه. وقيل: هم الزناة وأهل الفجور من قوله تعالى فَيَطْمَعَ الَّذِي فِي قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ. وَالْمُرْجِفُونَ ناس كانوا يرجفون بأخبار السوء عن سرايا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فيقولون: هزموا وقتلوا، وجرى عليهم كيت وكيت، فيكسرون بذلك قلوب المؤمنين. يقال: أرجف بكذا، إذا أخبر به على غير حقيقة، لكونه خبرا متزلزلا غير ثابت، من الرجفة وهي الزلزلة. والمعنى: لئن لم ينته المنافقون عن عداوتهم وكيدكم، والفسقة عن فجورهم، والمرجفون عما يؤلفون من أخبار السوء: لنأمرنك بأن تفعل بهم الأفاعيل التي تسوءهم وتنوؤهم «1» ، ثم بأن تضطرهم إلى طلب الجلاء عن المدينة، وإلى أن لا يساكنوك فيها إِلَّا زمنا قَلِيلًا ريثما يرتحلون ويلتقطون أنفسهم وعيالاتهم «2» ، فسمى ذلك إغراء، وهو التحريش على سبيل المجاز مَلْعُونِينَ نصب على الشتم أو الحال، أى: لا يجاورونك إلا ملعونين، دخل حرف الاستثناء على الظرف والحال معا، كما مرّ في قوله إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلى طَعامٍ غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إِناهُ ولا يصح أن ينتصب عن أُخِذُوا لأنّ ما بعد كلمة الشرط لا يعمل فيما قبلها. وقيل في قَلِيلًا وهو منصوب على الحال أيضا. ومعناه. لا يجاورونك إلا أقلاء أذلاء ملعونين.
Question
If you ask: what is the position of "they will not neighbor you"?
فإن قلت: ما موقع لا يجاورونك؟
Answer
I say: "they will not neighbor you" is coordinated with "We will surely incite you," because it is permissible for the oath to be answered with it. Do you not see the soundness of your saying: "If they do not cease, they will not neighbor you"?
قلت: لا يجاورونك عطف على لنغرينك، لأنه يجوز أن يجاب به القسم. ألا نرى إلى صحة قولك: لئن لم ينتهوا لا يجاورونك.
Question
If you ask: was it not proper for "they will not neighbor you" to be coordinated with "fa," and for it to be said "We will surely incite you against them, so they will not neighbor you"?
فإن قلت: أما كان من حق لا يجاورونك أن يعطف بالفاء، وأن يقال لنغرينك بهم فلا يجاورونك؟
Answer
I say: had the second been made a consequence of the first, the matter would be as you say; but it was made another answer to the oath coordinated with the first, and it was coordinated with "thumma" only because exile from the homelands was greater for them than all that had afflicted them, so its status was set apart from that of what it was coordinated with. "The way of God": in the place of a confirming verbal noun, that is: God established as a way, with those who feign [belief] toward the prophets, that they be killed wherever they are found. And from Muqātil: meaning as the people of Badr were killed and taken captive.
قلت: لو جعل الثاني مسببا عن الأوّل لكان الأمر كما قلت، ولكنه جعل جوابا آخر للقسم معطوفا على الأوّل، وإنما عطف بثم، لأن الجلاء عن الأوطان كان أعظم عليهم وأعظم من جميع ما أصيبوا به، فتراخت حاله عن حال المعطوف عليه سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ في موضع مصدر مؤكد، أى: سن الله في الذين ينافقون الأنبياء أن يقتلوا حيثما ثقفوا وعن مقاتل: يعنى كما قتل أهل بدر وأسروا.
Vol. 3, p. 562

2. . His statement "of what preceded from them of negligence [lit. 'of their cursing'], with repentance" [sic, as printed]: this is according to the Muʿtazila; or by mere grace according to Ahl al-Sunna. (ʿ)
1. (1) . أهلا بضيف أنى ما استفتح البابا
…. مجلبب من سواد الليل جلبابا لأبى زبيد. وأهلا: مفعول لمحذوف وجوبا، أى: أتيت أهلا. وبضيف: متعلق بمحذوف، أى. أرحب بضيف: ويجوز تعلقه بأهلا، لأن فيه معنى الترحيب. وما: مصدرية، أى: مدة استقامة الباب. والمراد منه التعميم، أى: في أى وقت يطلب فتح الباب: وصفه بالآتى في سواد الليل، مبالغة في التمدح بالكرم. ويجوز؟؟؟ أن الضيف محبوبته، فيكون الليل استزلها؟؟؟. وشبه استتار ضيفه بظلام الليل يلبس اللباس، والتجوز في الجلببة أو في الجلباب على طريق التصريحية، ويجوز لأن ما نافية، وعلى هذا فيصح أن يكون خطابا لملك الموت، حيث دخل ولم يطلب فتح الباب، وإن كان الضيف والحبيب قد يفعلان ذلك أيضا
2. . قوله «لما سلف لعنهن من التفريط مع التوبة» هذا عند المعتزلة. أو بمجرد الفضل عند أهل السنة. (ع)
Vol. 3, p. 561
1. (1). His statement "the deeds that distress them and weigh heavily upon them": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: it is said "I have with me what distressed him and weighed heavily upon him (sāʾahu wa-nāʾahu)," i.e., burdened him, and "what distresses him and weighs heavily upon him." Some said: he intended "sāʾahu" and "nāʾahu," and said "nāʾahu," though it is not transitive, only because of "sāʾahu," so that the speech would have a matching rhythm. (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: "What is meant by His saying Most High 'except for a little' is: just long enough for them to gather up their dependents and themselves, and no more." Aḥmad said: In it is an indication that whoever is legitimately required to vacate a house owned by another is granted a respite for a span of time, so that he may move himself, his belongings and his dependents, until another dwelling becomes available to him, by judgment [ijtihād]; and God knows best. [.....]
1. (1) . قوله «الأفاعيل التي تسوءهم وتنوؤهم» في الصحاح، يقال: له عندي ما ساءه وناءه، أى أثقله، وما يسوؤه وينوؤه، وقال بعضهم أراد ساءه وناءه وإنما قال ناءه وهو لا يتعدى لأجل ساءه، ليزدوج الكلام. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «المراد بقوله تعالى إِلَّا قَلِيلًا ريثما يلتقطون عيالاتهم وأنفسهم لا غير» قال أحمد: وفيها إشارة إلى أن من توجه عليه إخلاء منزل مملوك للغير بوجه شرعي، يمهل ربّما؟؟؟ ينتقل بنفسه ومتاعه وعياله برهة من الزمان، حتى يتحصل له منزل آخر على حسب الاجتهاد، والله أعلم. [.....]
Vol. 3, p. 562
1. (1). His statement "[with the verb belonging to] the Blaze": meaning: their faces, in the accusative. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «على أن الفعل للسعير، يعنى: وجوههم، بالنصب. (ع)
32
Q 33:63 · Vol. 3, p. 562

Verse 63

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"People ask you concerning the Hour. Say, 'Its knowledge is only with God.' And what would make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near. (63)
يَسْئَلُكَ النَّاسُ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ قُلْ إِنَّما عِلْمُها عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ تَكُونُ قَرِيباً (63)
Vol. 3, p. 562
" The polytheists used to ask the Messenger of God ﷺ about the time of the coming of the Hour, out of haste and by way of mockery, and the Jews used to ask him as a test, because God Most High had concealed its time in the Torah and in every scripture. So the Messenger of God ﷺ was commanded to answer them that it is knowledge God has reserved for Himself, not disclosing it to any angel or prophet; then He made clear to His Messenger that it is near in occurrence, as a threat to those in haste and a silencing of those testing. "Near": [meaning] something near; or because the "Hour" is in the sense of "the day," or in the sense of "a near time."
كان المشركون يسألون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن وقت قيام الساعة استعجالا على سبيل الهزء، واليهود يسألونه امتحانا، لأن الله تعالى عمى وقتها في التوراة وفي كل كتاب، فأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن يجيبهم بأنه علم قد استأثر الله به، لم يطلع عليه ملكا ولا نبيا، ثم بين لرسوله أنها قريبة الوقوع، تهديدا للمستعجلين، وإسكانا للممتحنين قَرِيباً شيئا قريبا. أو لأن الساعة في معنى اليوم، أو في زمان قريب.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 562

1. (1) . قوله «على أن الفعل للسعير، يعنى: وجوههم، بالنصب. (ع)

Q 33:64–65 · Vol. 3, p. 562

Verses 64 to 65

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze, (64) Abiding therein forever; they will not find a protector or a helper. (65)
إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَنَ الْكافِرِينَ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ سَعِيراً (64) خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً لا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا وَلا نَصِيراً (65)
Vol. 3, p. 562
" The "saʿīr": the fire that is kindled, intensely stoked.
السعير: النار المسعورة الشديدة الإيقاد.

Q 33:66 · Vol. 3, p. 562

Verse 66

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"On the Day their faces will be turned about in the Fire, they will say, 'Oh, we wish we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger!' (66)
يَوْمَ تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ يَقُولُونَ يا لَيْتَنا أَطَعْنَا اللَّهَ وَأَطَعْنَا الرَّسُولا (66)
Vol. 3, p. 562
" It has also been read "tuqallabu" [with the passive voice]; and "taqallabu" in the sense of "tataqallabu"; and "nuqallibu," that is, "We turn about"; and "taqallabu" [with the verb belonging to] the Blaze (1). The meaning of their being turned about: their being moved around in different directions, as you see a piece of meat turning in the pot when it boils and the boiling throws it from one side to another; or their being changed from their conditions and transformed from their forms; or their being cast into the Fire upside down, inverted. And the faces are specifically mentioned because the face is the most honored place on a person's body. It is also possible that "face" is an expression for the whole person. The governing element of the adverbial is "they say," or an omitted verb, which is "remember"; and if it is made accusative by the omitted verb, then "they say" is a circumstantial clause.
وقرئ: تقلب، على البناء للمفعول. وتقلب، بمعنى تتقلب. ونقلب، أى: نقلب نحن. وتقلب، على أن الفعل للسعير «1» . ومعنى تقليبها: تصريفها في الجهات، كما ترى البضعة تدور في القدر إذا غلت فترامى بها الغليان من جهة إلى جهة. أو تغييرها عن أحوالها وتحويلها عن هيئاتها. أو طرحها في النار مقلوبين منكوسين. وخصت الوجوه بالذكر، لأن الوجه أكرم موضع على الإنسان من جسده. ويجوز أن يكون الوجه عبارة عن الجملة، وناصب الظرف يَقُولُونَ أو محذوف. وهو «اذكر» وإذا نصب بالمحذوف كان يَقُولُونَ حالا.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 562

Q 33:67–68 · Vol. 3, pp. 562–563

Verses 67 to 68

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And they will say, 'Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they led us astray from the [right] way. (67) Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.' (68)
وَقالُوا رَبَّنا إِنَّا أَطَعْنا سادَتَنا وَكُبَراءَنا فَأَضَلُّونَا السَّبِيلا (67) رَبَّنا آتِهِمْ ضِعْفَيْنِ مِنَ الْعَذابِ وَالْعَنْهُمْ لَعْناً كَبِيراً (68)
Vol. 3, p. 562
" It has also been read "sādatanā" and "sādātinā": they are the leaders of disbelief who taught them disbelief and made it attractive to them. It is said "ḍalla l-sabīl" and "aḍallahu iyyāhu"; and the added alif is to lengthen the voice: the verse-endings were made like the rhyme-endings of poetry, its benefit being the pause and the indication that the speech has ended and that what follows is a new beginning. It has also been read "kathīran" [many], to multiply the number of curses; and "kabīran" [great], to indicate the severest and greatest curse. "Double": a double for their going astray and a double for their leading astray. They confess, and cry for help, and wish, and none of that benefits them.
وقرئ: سادتنا وساداتنا: وهم رؤساء الكفر الذين لقنوهم الكفر وزينوه لهم. يقال: ضلّ السبيل وأضله إياه، وزيادة الألف لإطلاق الصوت: جعلت فواصل الآي كقوافى الشعر، وفائدتها الوقف والدلالة على أن الكلام قد انقطع، وأن ما بعده مستأنف. وقرئ: كثيرا، تكثيرا لإعداد اللعائن. وكبيرا، ليدل على أشد اللعن وأعظمه ضِعْفَيْنِ ضعفا لضلاله وضعفا لإضلاله: يعترفون، ويستغيثون، ويتمنون، ولا ينفعهم شيء من ذلك.
Vol. 3, p. 563

1. (1) . قوله «على أن الفعل للسعير، يعنى: وجوههم، بالنصب. (ع)
Vol. 3, p. 563
1. (1). His statement "they blamed him for a defect": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "qarraftu the man," i.e., I found fault with him; and it is said "he is accused (yuqrafu) of such-and-such," i.e., you are cast with the sight of them [sic]. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "Do you not see that they called disgrace 'qāla'": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "this matter became a sabba [disgrace] upon him" (with ḍamma), i.e., a shame. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «وقيل قرفوه بعيب» في الصحاح: قرفت الرجل، أى: عبته، ويقال: هو يقرف بكذا، أى: ترمى برؤيتهم. (ع)

36
Q 33:69 · Vol. 3, p. 563

Verse 69

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"O you who have believed, be not like those who abused Moses; then God cleared him of what they said. And he was, in the sight of God, distinguished. (69)
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ آذَوْا مُوسى فَبَرَّأَهُ اللَّهُ مِمَّا قالُوا وَكانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَجِيهاً (69)
Vol. 3, p. 563
" "Be not like those who abused Moses": it was said: it was revealed concerning Zayd and Zaynab, and what was heard about it in the talk of some people. It was also said that the harming of Moses ﷺ was the story of the prostitute whom Qārūn wished to have accuse him falsely of [involvement with] her; it was said: their accusing him of killing Aaron, who had gone out with him to the mountain and died there; so the angels carried him and passed by them with him dead, and they saw him so that they knew he had not been killed. It was said: God revived him and he informed them of Moses' innocence ﷺ. It was said: they blamed him for a defect (1) in his body, such as leprosy or a hernia, so God made them aware that he was innocent of it. "Distinguished": possessing standing and rank with Him; for that reason He would remove accusations from him, repel harm, and protect him, lest any disgrace attach to him or he be described with a deficiency, as a king does for one who has closeness and standing with him. Ibn Masʿūd, al-Aʿmash and Abū Ḥaywa read: "and ʿAbdullāh was distinguished." Ibn Khālawayh said: I prayed behind Ibn Shannabūdh in the month of Ramaḍān and heard him recite it. But the reading of the majority is more fitting, because it conveys plainly his standing with God, like His saying Most High "with the Owner of the Throne, secure," whereas this [reading] is not like that. If you ask: His saying "of what they said" means "from their saying" or "from what was said," since "mā" is either verbal-noun forming or relative, and whichever it is, how can clearing from it be sound? I say: what is meant by the saying or the thing said is its import and content, which is the disgraceful matter. Do you not see that they called disgrace "qāla" (2), where "qāla" has the sense of "saying"?
لا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ آذَوْا مُوسى قيل: نزلت في شأن زيد وزينب، وما سمع فيه من قالة بعض الناس. وقيل: في أذى موسى عليه السلام: هو حديث المومسة التي أرادها قارون على قذفه بنفسها، وقيل: اتهامهم إياه بقتل هرون، وكان قد خرج معه الجبل فمات هناك، فحملته الملائكة ومروا به عليهم ميتا فأبصروه حتى عرفوا أنه غير مقتول. وقيل: أحياه الله فأخبرهم ببراءة موسى عليه السلام. وقيل: قرفوه بعيب «1» في جسده من برص أو أدرة، فأطلعهم الله على أنه بريء منه وَجِيهاً ذا جاه ومنزلة عنده، فلذلك كان يميط عنه التهم، ويدفع الأذى، ويحافظ عليه، لئلا يلحقه وصم ولا يوصف بنقيصة، كما يفعل الملك بمن له عنده قربة ووجاهة. وقرأ ابن مسعود والأعمش وأبو حيوة. وكان عبد الله وجيها. قال ابن خالويه: صليت خلف ابن شنبوذ في شهر رمضان، فسمعته يقرؤها. وقراءة العامة أوجه لأنها مفصحة عن وجاهته عند الله، كقوله تعالى عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ وهذه ليست كذلك. فإن قلت: قوله مِمَّا قالُوا معناه: من قولهم، أو من مقولهم، لأنّ «ما» إما مصدرية أو موصولة، وأيهما كان فكيف تصح البراءة منه؟ قلت المراد بالقول أو المقول: مؤداه ومضمونه، وهو الأمر المعيب. ألا ترى أنهم سموا السبة بالقالة «2» ، والقالة بمعنى القول؟
Editor’s notes on this page

2. . His statement "Do you not see that they called disgrace 'qāla'": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "this matter became a sabba [disgrace] upon him" (with ḍamma), i.e., a shame. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «وقيل قرفوه بعيب» في الصحاح: قرفت الرجل، أى: عبته، ويقال: هو يقرف بكذا، أى: ترمى برؤيتهم. (ع)

Q 33:70–73 · Vol. 3, pp. 563–565

Verses 70 to 73

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"O you who have believed, fear God and speak words of appropriate justice. (70) He will [then] amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment. (71) Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man [undertook to] bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. (72) [It was] so that God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women, and so that God may accept repentance from the believing men and believing women. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful. (73)
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَقُولُوا قَوْلاً سَدِيداً (70) يُصْلِحْ لَكُمْ أَعْمالَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ فازَ فَوْزاً عَظِيماً (71) إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا الْأَمانَةَ عَلَى السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَالْجِبالِ فَأَبَيْنَ أَنْ يَحْمِلْنَها وَأَشْفَقْنَ مِنْها وَحَمَلَهَا الْإِنْسانُ إِنَّهُ كانَ ظَلُوماً جَهُولاً (72) لِيُعَذِّبَ اللَّهُ الْمُنافِقِينَ وَالْمُنافِقاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكاتِ وَيَتُوبَ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً (73)
Vol. 3, p. 563
" "Words of appropriate justice": directed toward truth. "Sadād" is directing oneself toward the truth and speaking with justice. It is said "saddada the arrow toward the target" when one does not deviate it from its direction, as they say "an arrow that is straight (qāṣid)." What is meant: forbidding them from what they had plunged into
قَوْلًا سَدِيداً قاصدا إلى الحق والسداد: القصد إلى الحق، والقول بالعدل. يقال: سدّد السهم نحو الرميّة: إذا لم يعدل به عن سمتها، كما قالوا: سهم قاصد، والمراد: نهيهم عما خاضوا
Vol. 3, p. 564
regarding the story of Zaynab without intention and with justice in speech, and urging that their speech be made upright in every matter, because guarding the tongue and uprightness of speech is the head of all good. And the meaning: be mindful of God in guarding your tongues and setting your speech straight, for if you do that God will give you the utmost of what is sought: the acceptance of your good deeds and recompense for them, and the forgiveness of your misdeeds and their expiation. It was also said: the amendment of deeds is the success [granted] in bringing them forth righteous and pleasing. And this verse confirms the one before it: that one was built on the prohibition of what harms the Messenger of God, may God Most High bless him and grant him peace, and this one on the command to fear God Most High in guarding the tongue, so that prohibition and command follow upon them in succession, the prohibition being followed by what contains the threat in the story of Moses ﷺ and the command being followed by the emphatic promise, so that what turns [one] away from harm and what calls to abandoning it are strengthened. When He said "And whoever obeys God and His Messenger" and tied the great attainment to obedience, He followed it with His saying "Indeed, We offered the Trust," and by the Trust He means obedience, magnifying its importance and exalting its station. There are two aspects to this. The first: that these great bodies, the heavens, the earth and the mountains, submitted to God's command with the submission appropriate to the like of them (which is what can come from inanimate things), and obeyed Him with the obedience that is valid for them and fitting for them, in that they did not refuse His will and volition in being brought into existence, formed, and fashioned in varied configurations and diverse shapes, as He said "They said, 'We have come willingly.'" But man's condition, with respect to the acts of obedience valid from him and the submission to God's commands and prohibitions fitting for him, he being a rational living being fit for obligation, was not like the condition of those inanimate things with respect to the submission and non-refusal valid for them and fitting for them. And what is meant by the Trust is obedience, because it is necessarily owed, just as a trust is necessarily to be returned. And its being offered to inanimate things, and their declining and fearing: figurative. As for the bearing of the Trust, it is from your saying: so-and-so is a bearer of the trust and one who carries it, meaning that he does not return it to its owner until it leaves his liability and he is discharged from its burden, because the trust is as if it were riding upon the one entrusted with it, and he is its bearer. Do you not see that they say: "Debts have mounted him" and "I have a right against him"; so when he discharges it, it no longer rides him nor does he bear it. Similar is their saying: "A patron does not possess [help] over a patron," meaning that he gives his help freely and is generous with it, not withholding it as the one who forsakes withholds it. And of this is the saying of the poet: "Your brother is he whose own self does not hold back its tenderness, and who shakes with rage at the things that anger [you]" (2) — that is, he does not hold back compassion and affection as the stingy owner holds back what is in his hand, but gives it and is generous with it. And of this is their saying "hate the due of your brother," because when he loves it he does not bring it out to his brother or discharge it, and when he hates it he brings it out and discharges it,
فيه من حديث زينب من غير قصد وعدل في القول، والبعث على أن يسد قولهم «1» في كل باب لأنّ حفظ اللسان وسداد القول رأس الخير كله. والمعنى: راقبوا الله في حفظ ألسنتكم، وتسديد قولكم، فإنكم إن فعلتم ذلك أعطاكم الله ما هو غاية الطلبة من تقبل حسناتكم والإثابة عليها، ومن مغفرة سيئاتكم وتكفيرها. وقيل إصلاح الأعمال التوفيق في المجيء بها صالحة مرضية وهذه الآية مقرّرة للتي قبلها، بنيت تلك على النهى عما يؤذى رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم، وهذه على الأمر باتقاء الله تعالى في حفظ اللسان، ليترادف عليهم النهى والأمر، مع اتباع النهى ما يتضمن الوعيد من قصة موسى عليه السلام، وإتباع الأمر الوعد البليغ فيقوى الصارف عن الأذى والداعي إلى تركه. لما قال وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وعلق بالطاعة الفوز العظيم، أتبعه قوله إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا الْأَمانَةَ وهو يريد بالأمانة الطاعة، فعظم أمرها وفخم شأنها، وفيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنّ هذه الأجرام العظام من السماوات والأرض والجبال قد انقادت لأمر الله عز وعلا انقياد مثلها- وهو ما يتأتى من الجمادات- وأطاعت له الطاعة التي تصح منها وتليق بها- حيث لم تمتنع على مشيئته وإرادته إيجادا وتكوينا وتسوية على هيآت مختلفة وأشكال متنوعة، كما قال قالَتا أَتَيْنا طائِعِينَ وأما الإنسان فلم تكن حاله- فيما يصح منه من الطاعات ويليق به من الانقياد لأوامر الله ونواهيه، وهو حيوان عاقل صالح للتكليف- مثل حال تلك الجمادات فيما يصح منها ويليق بها من الانقياد وعدم الامتناع، والمراد بالأمانة: الطاعة، لأنها لازمة الوجود، كما أن الأمانة لازمة الأداء. وعرضها على الجمادات وإباؤها وإشفاقها: مجاز. وأما حمل الأمانة فمن قولك: فلان حامل للأمانة ومحتمل لها، تريد: أنه لا يؤديها إلى صاحبها حتى تزول عن ذمّته ويخرج عن عهدتها لأن الأمانة كأنها راكبة للمؤتمن عليها وهو حاملها. ألا تراهم يقولون: ركبته الديون، ولى عليه حق، فإذا أداها لم تبق راكبة له ولا هو حاملا لها. ونحوه قولهم، لا يملك مولى لمولى نصرا. يريدون: أنه يبذل النصرة له ويسامحه بها، ولا يمسكها كما يمسكها الخاذل. ومنه قول القائل: أخوك الّذى لا تملك الحسّ نفسه … وترفضّ عند المحفظات الكتائف «2» أى لا يمسك الرقة والعطف إمساك المالك الضنين ما في يده، بل يبذل ذلك ويسمح به. ومنه قولهم ابغض حق أخيك؟ لأنه إذا أحبه لم يخرجه إلى أخيه ولم يؤده، وإذا أبغضه أخرجه وأدّاه،
Vol. 3, p. 565
so the meaning is: "they declined to bear it and man bore it": they declined except to discharge it, and man declined except to be one who carries it without discharging it. Then He described him as unjust for being one who abandons the discharge of the trust, and as ignorant for his erring in what would bring him happiness though he was able to do it, namely its discharge. The second: that what man was charged with reached such a degree of greatness and heaviness of burden that it was offered to the greatest, strongest and most powerful of what God created of bodies, [asking] that they bear it and take it on single-handedly, and they refused to bear it and take it on single-handedly and feared it, and man bore it despite his weakness and the softness of his strength. "Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant" in that he bore the trust and then did not fulfill it, and guaranteed it and then proved treacherous (1) to his guarantee concerning it. And the like of this speech is abundant in the language of the Arabs, and the Qurʾān came only according to their ways and styles. Of that is their saying: "If fat were asked: where are you going? it would say: to straighten the crookedness," and how many examples they have in the mouths of beasts and inanimate things. And picturing a conversation of fat is impossible, but the purpose is that fatness in an animal improves its ugliness, just as leanness makes its beauty ugly; so he pictured the effect of fatness in it with a depiction that is more telling to the listener's soul, more familiar to it, more welcomed by it, and more informative of its reality. Likewise the depiction of the greatness of the trust, the difficulty of its matter, the heaviness of bearing it and of fulfilling it.
فمعنى: فأبين أن يحملنها وحملها الإنسان، فأبين إلا أن يؤدينها وأبى الإنسان إلا أن يكون محتملا لها لا يؤديها. ثم وصفه بالظلم لكونه تاركا لأداء الأمانة، وبالجهل لإخطائه ما يسعده مع تمكنه منه وهو أداؤها. والثاني: أن ما كلفه الإنسان بلغ من عظمه وثقل محمله: أنه عرض على أعظم ما خلق الله من الأجرام وأقواه وأشدّه: أن يتحمله ويستقل به، فأبى حمله والاستقلال به وأشفق منه، وحمله الإنسان على ضعفه ورخاوة قوّته إِنَّهُ كانَ ظَلُوماً جَهُولًا حيث حمل الأمانة ثم لم يف بها، وضمنها ثم خاس «1» بضمانه فيها، ونحو هذا من الكلام كثير في لسان العرب. وما جاء القرآن إلا على طرقهم وأساليبهم من ذلك قولهم: لو قيل للشحم: أين تذهب؟ لقال: أسوى العوج، وكم وكم لهم من أمثال على ألسنة البهائم والجمادات. وتصوّر مقاولة الشحم محال، ولكن الغرض أنّ السمن في الحيوان مما يحسن قبيحه، كما أن العجف مما يقبح حسنه، فصوّر أثر السمن فيه تصويرا هو أوقع في نفس السامع، وهي به آنس وله أقبل، وعلى حقيقته أوقف، وكذلك تصوير عظم الأمانة وصعوبة أمرها وثقل محملها والوفاء بها.
Question
If you ask: the aspect of the similitude is known in their saying to one who does not hold to a single opinion: "I see you putting one foot forward and holding back the other," because his state, in his vacillating and wavering between two opinions and his not going ahead with either, was likened to the state of one who hesitates in his going and does not bring his feet together to proceed in his direction. Each of the likened and that to which it is likened is something sound, falling under validity and knowledge; and that is not the case with what is in this verse, for the offering of the trust to an inanimate thing and its declining and fearing is impossible in itself, not sound; so how is the building of a similitude upon the impossible valid, and what is an example of this but your likening something while that to which it is likened is inconceivable?
فإن قلت: قد علم وجه التمثيل في قولهم للذي لا يثبت على رأى واحد: أراك تقدم رجلا وتؤخر أخرى، لأنه مثلت حاله- في تميله وترجحه بين الرأيين وتركه المضي على أحدهما- بحال من يتردد في ذهابه فلا يجمع رجليه للمضى في وجهه. وكل واحد من الممثل والممثل به شيء مستقيم داخل تحت الصحة والمعرفة، وليس كذلك ما في هذه الآية، فإن عرض الأمانة على الجماد وإباءه وإشفاقه محال في نفسه، غير مستقيم، فكيف صح بناء التمثيل على المحال، وما مثال هذا إلا أن تشبه شيئا والمشبه به غير معقول.
Answer
I say: that to which it is likened in the verse, and in their saying "if fat were asked where are you going," and in their parallels, is supposed; and suppositions are imagined in the mind just as realities are: the state of obligation, in its difficulty and the heaviness of bearing it, was likened to its supposed state had it been offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, in which case they would have declined to bear it and feared it. And the lām in "so that He may punish" is the lām of causation by way of figurative usage, because punishment is the outcome of bearing the Trust, just as discipline in "I struck him for discipline" is the outcome of the striking. Al-Aʿmash read "wa-yatūbu" [with the verb in the indicative], to make the cause limited to the act of the bearer, and he begins anew: "and God accepts repentance" (2). And the meaning of the reading of the majority: that God may punish the bearer of the Trust and accept repentance from others who did not bear it, because when repentance is accepted from the one who fulfills, that is a kind of punishment of the betrayer; and God knows best. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever recites Sūrat al-Aḥzāb and teaches it to his family and those his right hand possesses, will be given security from the punishment of the grave" (3).
قلت: الممثل به في الآية وفي قولهم: لو قيل للشحم أين تذهب. وفي نظائره مفروض، والمفروضات تتخيل في الذهن كما المحققات: مثلت حال التكليف في صعوبته وثقل محمله بحاله المفروضة لو عرضت على السماوات والأرض والجبال لأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها. واللام في لِيُعَذِّبَ لام التعليل على طريق المجاز، لأنّ التعذيب نتيجة حمل الأمانة، كما أن التأديب في ضربته للتأديب نتيجة الضرب. وقرأ الأعمش. ويتوب، ليجعل العلة قاصرة على فعل الحامل، ويبتدئ: ويتوب الله «2» . ومعنى قراءة العامة: ليعذب الله حامل الأمانة ويتوب على غيره ممن لم يحملها، لأنه إذا تيب على الوافي كان ذلك نوعا من عذاب الغادر، والله أعلم. قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة الأحزاب وعلمها أهله وما ملكت يمينه، أعطى الأمان من عذاب القبر «3» » .
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 3, p. 563
1. (1). His statement "they blamed him for a defect": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "qarraftu the man," i.e., I found fault with him; and it is said "he is accused (yuqrafu) of such-and-such," i.e., you are cast with the sight of them [sic]. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "Do you not see that they called disgrace 'qāla'": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "this matter became a sabba [disgrace] upon him" (with ḍamma), i.e., a shame. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «وقيل قرفوه بعيب» في الصحاح: قرفت الرجل، أى: عبته، ويقال: هو يقرف بكذا، أى: ترمى برؤيتهم. (ع)
2. . قوله «ألا ترى أنهم سموا السبة بالقالة» في الصحاح: صار هذا الأمر سبة عليه- بالضم، أى: عارا (ع)
Vol. 3, p. 564
1. (1). His statement "that their speech be made upright": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "his speech was straightened (sadda)," with kasra: i.e., it became upright. (ʿ)
2. . By al-Quṭāmī; and it was said: by Dhū l-Rumma. "Ḥassa lahu ḥassan": he softened toward him and sympathized. "Al-ḥiss" is also: intelligence, planning, and consideration of consequences. "Al-irfiḍāḍ" is from sprinkling and scattering; "aḥfaẓahu iḥfāẓan": he angered him; so "al-muḥfiẓāt" are the things that anger; and "al-katāʾif" is the plural of "katīfa," which is rancor and malice. He says: your brother is the one whose self does not possess mercy but gives it to you; or whose self is not able to deliberate slowly but hastens to you suddenly; and his rancors tremble and disappear from your side at matters that anger you, because they anger him too.
1. (1) . قوله «على ان يسد قولهم» في الصحاح: سد قوله يسدّ- بالكسر-: أى صار سديدا. (ع)
2. . للقطامى. وقبل: لذي الرمة. وحس له حسا: رق له وعطف. والحس أيضا: العقل والتدبير والنظر في العواقب، والارفضاض من الترشرش والتناثر، وأحفظه إحفاظا: أغضبه، فالمحفظات: المغضبات. والكتائف: جمع كتيفة، وهي الضغينة والحقد. يقول: أخوك هو الذي لا تملك نفسه الرحمة، بل يبذلها لك. أو لا تقدر نفسه على التدبر بالتأنى، بل يسرع إليك بغتة وترتعد وتذهب ضغائنه من جهتك عند الأمور المغضبة لك، لأنها تغضبه أيضا.
Vol. 3, p. 565
1. (1). His statement "then proved treacherous to his guarantee concerning it": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "khāsa bihi yakhīsu and yakhūsu," i.e., he betrayed him; it is said "khāsa bi-l-ʿahd" when he broke it. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "wa-yatūbu": i.e., with the indicative ending (raf'), as in al-Nasafī. (ʿ)
3. . Narrated by al-Thaʿlabī and Ibn Mardawayh from the ḥadīth of Ubayy b. Kaʿb ؓ.
1. (1) . قوله «ثم خاس بضمانه فيها» في الصحاح: خاس به يخيس ويخوس، أى: غدر به يقال: خاص بالعهد، إذ نكث. (ع)
2. . قوله «ويتوب» أى بالرفع، كما في النسفي. (ع)
3. . أخرجه الثعلبي وابن مردويه من حديث أبى بن كعب رضى الله عنه.
